description: Foundation of mathematical reasoning. Covers the real number system, variables, equations, inequalities, polynomials, rational and radical expressions, quadratics, and an introduction to functions.

concepts.title: Real Number System
learning_objectives: Classify numbers as natural, whole, integer, rational, or irrational
Place real numbers on a number line
Identify the properties of real numbers: commutative, associative, distributive, identity, and inverse

concepts.title: Order of Operations
learning_objectives: Evaluate numerical expressions using the standard order of operations (PEMDAS)
Simplify expressions containing nested grouping symbols
Identify and correct common order-of-operations errors

concepts.title: Absolute Value and Distance
learning_objectives: Compute the absolute value of any real number
Interpret absolute value as distance from zero on the number line
Calculate the distance between two points on a number line using absolute value

concepts.title: Properties of Integer Exponents
learning_objectives: Evaluate expressions with positive, negative, and zero exponents
Apply the product rule, quotient rule, and power rule for integer exponents
Convert between standard notation and scientific notation

concepts.title: Operations with Signed Numbers
learning_objectives: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide positive and negative rational numbers
Apply the rules of signs in multi-step calculations
Evaluate expressions involving combinations of signed-number operations

concepts.title: Variables and Algebraic Expressions
learning_objectives: Translate verbal phrases into algebraic expressions
Evaluate algebraic expressions by substituting given values for variables
Distinguish between expressions, equations, and identities

concepts.title: Combining Like Terms
learning_objectives: Identify like terms in an algebraic expression
Simplify expressions by combining like terms
Rearrange and group terms to simplify multi-variable expressions

concepts.title: Distributive Property
learning_objectives: Apply the distributive property to expand expressions
Combine distribution with like-term collection to simplify expressions
Extend the distributive property to expressions with multiple grouping levels

concepts.title: Evaluating and Simplifying Formulas
learning_objectives: Evaluate common formulas (area, perimeter, temperature conversion) for given inputs
Rearrange simple formulas to solve for a specified variable
Identify domain restrictions on formulas involving division or square roots

concepts.title: Solving One-Variable Linear Equations
learning_objectives: Solve linear equations using inverse operations
Solve equations that require distribution and combining like terms
Verify solutions by substituting back into the original equation

concepts.title: Equations with Fractions and Decimals
learning_objectives: Clear fractions from an equation by multiplying by the least common denominator
Solve equations containing decimal coefficients
Determine whether an equation is conditional, an identity, or a contradiction

concepts.title: Literal Equations and Formulas
learning_objectives: Solve a literal equation for a specified variable
Rearrange physics and geometry formulas to isolate any variable
Apply formula rearrangement to unit-conversion and rate problems

concepts.title: Linear Word Problems
learning_objectives: Define a variable and set up a linear equation from a word problem
Solve mixture, rate, and consecutive-integer problems
Interpret and validate the solution in the original problem context

concepts.title: Proportions and Variation
learning_objectives: Solve proportions using cross-multiplication
Model and solve direct-variation and inverse-variation problems
Apply proportional reasoning to scale and similar-figure problems

concepts.title: Solving Linear Inequalities
learning_objectives: Solve one-variable linear inequalities, reversing the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative
Express solutions in interval notation and graph them on a number line
Translate inequality word problems into mathematical statements and solve them

concepts.title: Compound Inequalities
learning_objectives: Solve compound inequalities joined by AND (intersection)
Solve compound inequalities joined by OR (union)
Graph compound inequality solution sets and express them in interval notation

concepts.title: Absolute Value Equations
learning_objectives: Solve equations of the form |ax + b| = c by splitting into two cases
Identify absolute value equations that have no solution
Solve absolute value equations with expressions on both sides

concepts.title: Absolute Value Inequalities
learning_objectives: Solve |ax + b| < c as a compound AND inequality
Solve |ax + b| > c as a compound OR inequality
Graph solutions and express them in interval notation

concepts.title: The Coordinate Plane
learning_objectives: Plot and identify ordered pairs in all four quadrants
Calculate the distance between two points using the distance formula
Find the midpoint of a line segment given its endpoints

concepts.title: Slope of a Line
learning_objectives: Calculate slope from two points using the slope formula
Interpret slope as a rate of change in applied contexts
Classify lines as having positive, negative, zero, or undefined slope

concepts.title: Slope-Intercept Form
learning_objectives: Write a linear equation in slope-intercept form y = mx + b
Graph a line given its slope and y-intercept
Convert a linear equation from standard form to slope-intercept form

concepts.title: Point-Slope and Standard Forms
learning_objectives: Write a linear equation in point-slope form given a point and a slope
Convert between slope-intercept, point-slope, and standard form
Write the equation of a line passing through two given points

concepts.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
learning_objectives: Determine whether two lines are parallel, perpendicular, or neither from their slopes
Write the equation of a line parallel to a given line through a given point
Write the equation of a line perpendicular to a given line through a given point

concepts.title: Solving Systems by Graphing
learning_objectives: Graph two linear equations on the same coordinate plane and identify the intersection point
Classify a system as having one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions from its graph
Estimate solutions of systems from graphs and verify algebraically

concepts.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
learning_objectives: Solve a system of two linear equations using the substitution method
Choose the most efficient variable to isolate for substitution
Identify inconsistent and dependent systems algebraically

concepts.title: Solving Systems by Elimination
learning_objectives: Solve a system of two linear equations using the addition/elimination method
Multiply one or both equations to create opposite coefficients before adding
Select substitution or elimination based on the structure of the system

concepts.title: Applications of Systems
learning_objectives: Set up and solve mixture, rate-time, and break-even problems as systems
Model real-world scenarios with two variables and two constraints
Interpret the solution of a system in the context of the application

concepts.title: Systems of Linear Inequalities
learning_objectives: Graph a linear inequality in two variables and shade the solution region
Graph a system of linear inequalities and identify the feasible region
Determine whether a given point lies in the solution set of a system of inequalities

concepts.title: Rules of Exponents
learning_objectives: Apply product, quotient, power-of-a-power, and power-of-a-product rules
Simplify expressions with negative and zero exponents
Combine multiple exponent rules in a single expression

concepts.title: Introduction to Polynomials
learning_objectives: Identify monomials, binomials, and trinomials and state their degree
Write polynomials in standard form (descending order of degree)
Evaluate polynomials for given values of the variable

concepts.title: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
learning_objectives: Add polynomials by combining like terms
Subtract polynomials by distributing the negative sign and combining like terms
Simplify polynomial expressions involving multiple additions and subtractions

concepts.title: Multiplying Polynomials
learning_objectives: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
Multiply two binomials using the FOIL method or distribution
Multiply any two polynomials using the distributive property

concepts.title: Special Products
learning_objectives: Expand the square of a binomial: (a + b)² and (a − b)²
Expand the product of conjugates: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²
Recognize and apply special product patterns to simplify computation

concepts.title: Greatest Common Factor and Factoring by Grouping
learning_objectives: Identify and factor out the greatest common factor (GCF) from a polynomial
Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping
Recognize when a polynomial is prime (cannot be factored)

concepts.title: Factoring Trinomials (Leading Coefficient 1)
learning_objectives: Factor trinomials of the form x² + bx + c by finding two integers whose product is c and sum is b
Factor trinomials that require extraction of a GCF before factoring
Determine when a trinomial with leading coefficient 1 is not factorable over the integers

concepts.title: Factoring Trinomials (Leading Coefficient ≠ 1)
learning_objectives: Factor trinomials of the form ax² + bx + c using the ac-method or trial and error
Apply grouping after splitting the middle term in the ac-method
Combine GCF extraction with advanced trinomial factoring

concepts.title: Factoring Special Forms
learning_objectives: Factor a difference of two squares: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
Factor a perfect square trinomial: a² ± 2ab + b² = (a ± b)²
Factor sums and differences of cubes: a³ ± b³

concepts.title: General Factoring Strategy
learning_objectives: Apply a systematic factoring strategy: GCF first, then recognize the form
Factor polynomials that require multiple factoring techniques in sequence
Verify factoring results by multiplication

concepts.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
learning_objectives: Identify values of the variable that make a rational expression undefined
Simplify rational expressions by factoring and cancelling common factors
Distinguish between legitimate cancellation and common errors

concepts.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions
learning_objectives: Multiply rational expressions by factoring, cancelling, and then multiplying
Divide rational expressions by multiplying by the reciprocal
Simplify complex fractions involving polynomial expressions

concepts.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions
learning_objectives: Find the least common denominator (LCD) of two rational expressions
Add and subtract rational expressions with unlike denominators
Simplify the result of addition or subtraction by factoring

concepts.title: Solving Rational Equations
learning_objectives: Solve equations containing rational expressions by multiplying through by the LCD
Identify and exclude extraneous solutions
Solve applied problems involving rates, work, and proportions

concepts.title: Simplifying Radical Expressions
learning_objectives: Simplify square roots by factoring out perfect-square factors
Simplify nth roots using the product and quotient rules for radicals
Convert between radical notation and rational exponent notation

concepts.title: Operations with Radicals
learning_objectives: Add and subtract like radical expressions
Multiply radical expressions, including binomials containing radicals
Simplify products and sums of radicals into simplest radical form

concepts.title: Rationalizing Denominators
learning_objectives: Rationalize a denominator containing a single radical term
Rationalize a denominator containing a binomial with radicals using conjugates
Simplify expressions after rationalization

concepts.title: Solving Radical Equations
learning_objectives: Solve equations containing one or two radical terms by isolating and squaring
Identify and reject extraneous solutions introduced by squaring
Solve radical equations involving rational exponents

concepts.title: Solving Quadratics by Factoring
learning_objectives: Apply the zero-product property to solve factored quadratic equations
Factor and solve quadratic equations of the form ax² + bx + c = 0
Solve equations reducible to quadratic form by factoring

concepts.title: Completing the Square
learning_objectives: Transform a quadratic expression into the form (x + p)² + q
Solve quadratic equations by completing the square
Derive the vertex of a parabola by completing the square

concepts.title: The Quadratic Formula
learning_objectives: Apply the quadratic formula to solve any quadratic equation
Use the discriminant to determine the number and type of solutions
Select the most efficient method for solving a given quadratic equation

concepts.title: Graphing Quadratic Functions
learning_objectives: Identify the vertex, axis of symmetry, and direction of opening of a parabola
Graph a quadratic function using its vertex and intercepts
Convert between standard form and vertex form of a quadratic function

concepts.title: Applications of Quadratics
learning_objectives: Model projectile motion and area optimization problems with quadratic equations
Determine maximum or minimum values using the vertex
Interpret quadratic solutions in real-world contexts

concepts.title: Function Notation and Evaluation
learning_objectives: Determine whether a relation is a function using the vertical line test
Evaluate functions using function notation f(x)
Interpret function notation in applied contexts

concepts.title: Domain and Range
learning_objectives: Determine the domain and range of a function from its equation
Identify domain restrictions from denominators and even roots
Express domain and range in interval notation

concepts.title: Function Operations and Composition
learning_objectives: Compute the sum, difference, product, and quotient of two functions
Evaluate and simplify the composition of two functions (f ∘ g)(x)
Determine the domain of a composite function

concepts.title: Inverse Functions
learning_objectives: Determine whether a function is one-to-one using the horizontal line test
Find the inverse of a one-to-one function algebraically
Verify that two functions are inverses by showing f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x

concepts.title: Transformations of Functions
learning_objectives: Identify and apply vertical and horizontal shifts to function graphs
Identify and apply reflections across the x-axis and y-axis
Identify and apply vertical and horizontal stretches and compressions

projects.title: Derive the Quadratic Formula
projects.description: Starting from the general quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, derive the quadratic formula by completing the square. Explain each step and justify why the discriminant determines the nature of the solutions.
learning_objectives: Apply the completing the square technique to a general quadratic
Construct a step-by-step algebraic derivation
Explain the role of the discriminant in determining solution types

projects.title: Break-Even Analysis for a Small Business
projects.description: Model a small business scenario with revenue and cost as linear functions. Find the break-even point using a system of equations, then extend the model with a quadratic revenue curve and analyze profit maximization.
learning_objectives: Set up linear cost and revenue functions from a word problem
Solve a system of equations to find the break-even point
Use quadratic optimization to determine maximum profit

projects.title: Cryptography with Function Composition
projects.description: Design a simple substitution cipher using function composition. Create an encoding function and its inverse decoding function, then prove they are true inverses.
learning_objectives: Model a real-world encoding process as a function
Compose functions to build multi-step transformations
Derive and verify an inverse function

projects.title: Projectile Motion Investigation
projects.description: Analyze the trajectory of a launched projectile. Derive the height function from given initial conditions, find maximum height, time of flight, and range. Present results with graphs and interpretations.
learning_objectives: Model a physical scenario with a quadratic function
Calculate vertex coordinates and interpret them as max height and optimal time
Graph the trajectory and annotate key features
